title: āditta sutta
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.

paras.en: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Gayā, at Gayā’s Head, together with a thousand bhikkhus. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Bhikkhus, all is burning.

And what, bhikkhus, is the all that is burning?
The eye is burning, visual forms are burning,
eye-consciousness is burning,
eye-contact is burning,
and whatever is felt with eye-contact as condition — whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that too is burning.

Burning with what? Burning with the fire of craving, with the fire of aversion, with the fire of delusion; burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and misery, I say.

The ear is burning … The nose is burning …
The tongue is burning … The body is burning …

The mind is burning, mental objects are burning, mind-consciousness is burning,
mind-contact is burning, and whatever is felt with mind-contact as condition —
whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that too is burning.

Burning with what? Burning with the fire of craving, with the fire of aversion, with the fire of delusion; burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and misery, I say.

Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple experiences disenchantment towards the eye, towards visual forms, towards eye-consciousness, towards eye-contact, towards whatever is felt with eye-contact as condition — whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant; …
towards the mind … towards whatever is felt with mind-contact as condition — whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant;

Experiencing disenchantment, he becomes free from attachment. Through the fading of attachment,
he is liberated. When he is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘liberated.’
He understands: ‘Birth is finished with, the spiritual life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”

This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement. And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the thousand bhikkhus were liberated from the āsavas by non-clinging.”
